subject: Operationalization checklist + request: sample traffic capture and sizing inputs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena@parcelbright.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Operationalization checklist + request: sample traffic capture and sizing inputs

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo today; good conversation. Below is a short post-call recap and a concrete ask so our infra team can produce a realistic sizing estimate and pilot plan. We want to confirm the traffic profile and the latency SLOs before we propose capacity.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: customer-facing chat (text + short context documents). Mix: ~85% non-streaming, ~15% streaming (progressive deliver).
- Target latency SLOs you mentioned: median ~120–150ms, p95 <= 350ms for interactive flows.
- Expected steady-state: 40 QPS with average 180 tokens/request; peak crest: 280 QPS sustained for ~5–10m bursts; token burst up to 3x on holiday loads.
- Concurrency: typical session concurrency ~0.6 per user; simultaneous open sessions peak ~1,400.

Asks (what we need from ParcelBright)
1) Small sample capture: 24–72 hours of anonymized request headers and payload size/activity metrics. Prefer CSV or newline JSON with fields: timestamp, request_type (streaming|non-streaming), tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, region. If you can’t share payloads, schema + histograms are fine.
2) Confirm percent of streaming vs non-streaming by traffic (we used 15% in the call).
3) Clarify the worst-case conversation length (max tokens) and how often clients request forced-retry (rate of client replays).
4) Any hard SLA blockers: p99 expectation? data residency constraints?

What we'll deliver (next from Redwood)
- A sizing note: tokens/sec and GPU-slot recommendation, plus expected p95 latency envelope under steady vs crest.
- A simple pilot canary plan (2-week pilot, canary routing, and fallback model variant).
- Draft SLO spreadsheet for sign-off (attached: slo-draft.xlsx).

Tentative next steps / owners
- ParcelBright: deliver sample capture + confirmation of streaming mix (owner: Elena) — due EOD Thu 6/17 if possible.
- Redwood: initial sizing note + pilot outline (owner: Marissa/Rishi) — target Tue 6/22.

Attachments: slo-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet with suggested p50/p95 targets, measurement plan)

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Elena Novak <elena@parcelbright.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Greene <tom.greene@parcelbright.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operationalization checklist + request: sample traffic capture and sizing inputs

Thanks Marissa — that lines up with what we discussed. Quick clarifications and we're attaching the first capture export.

Clarifications
- Streaming: closer to 18% of requests (progressive response used by mobile app).
- Steady-state: closer to 45 QPS; peaks are occasional but predictable (marketing emails). Crest events have hit 320 QPS historically for ~6m.
- Max tokens: most sessions sit under 800 tokens, but ~2% of sessions exceed 2,400 tokens (long support threads).
- No p99 SLA today; we want p95 to be our operational SLO.
- Data residency: US only for PII traffic; anonymized telemetry is fine to share.

Attachment: traffic-sample-1.csv (CSV export, 48KB) — contains 48 hours of request lines (timestamp,req_type,tokens_in,tokens_out,latency_ms,region) with user and content fields removed.

We can try to get a larger 7-day export but that will take a little more time; this 48h sample should help you size.

Elena
ParcelBright

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Novak <elena@parcelbright.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operationalization checklist + request: sample traffic capture and sizing inputs

Elena — perfect, thanks for the quick turn. Monica and I pulled the CSV and started a quick pass. Two immediate asks to help accuracy:

1) Can you include a small sampling of sequence-length histograms (requests bucketed by tokens: <128, 128-512, 512-1024, 1024-2048, >2048)? That helps with KV-cache and attention planning.
2) For streaming, can you indicate average chunk size (tokens per chunk) and typical chunk cadence (tokens/sec per connection)?

Preliminary notes from our look (very rough)
- Median tokens/request in the capture: ~165.
- Observed crest in the window: 308 QPS for ~3m (aligns with your crest numbers).
- Streaming sessions show small chunks (~20–30 tokens) every ~250–400ms on average.

Rishi and I will produce a two-page sizing note: tokens/sec demand, projected GPU-slot counts with padding for burst, and an outline of a 2-week canary. Rishi — if you can add a note on how we treat streaming connections for slot accounting (KV cache pinning vs ephemeral), that will be helpful.

Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Elena Novak <elena@parcelbright.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operationalization checklist + request: sample traffic capture and sizing inputs

Thanks — quick engineering note and what we'll include in the sizing doc.

Engineering assumptions we plan to use
- Baseline model: 13B quantized; alternate fallback: 6B quantized for heavy-burst preservation.
- We assume average decode length = tokens_out = 160 in steady-state; peak token/sec computed from observed QPS * avg tokens per request plus streaming chunk overhead.
- Streaming accounting: we will account for streaming connections as an active slot while the session maintains rapid chunk cadence (>1 chunk/sec). For your measured cadence (~2.5 chunks/sec), we'll count as full active slot for ~50–70% of the session duration.
- KV cache sizing: we will conservatively provision for session retention for long threads (the ~2% >2400 tokens); we can propose a tiered policy to evict rarely-accessed long sessions after 24h to save memory.

Planned deliverables (by Tue 6/22)
- tokens/sec profile: steady vs crest vs extreme holiday multipliers
- GPU-slot recommendation with headroom for 3x crest (for safety) and expected p95 latency envelopes for each mode
- Canary plan: routing rules, traffic cutover steps, rollback criteria, and measurement dashboards (latency, token-cost, error rates)

If Elena/Tom can add those histograms and streaming chunk metrics, we can tighten GPU counts by ~20% vs our conservative estimate.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
